questions.text:
A variable x is said to be live at a statement [latex]S_{i}[/latex] in a program if the following three conditions hold simultaneously:
i. There exists a statement [latex]S_{j}[/latex] that uses x
ii. There is a path from [latex]S_{i}[/latex] to [latex]S_{j}[/latex] in the flow graph corresponding to the program
iii. The path has no intervening assignment to x including at [latex]S_{i}[/latex] and [latex]S_{j}[/latex]

The variables which are live both at the statement in basic block 2 and at the statement in basic block 3 of the above control flow graph are
questions.solution:
Live-in = use [latex]\cup[/latex] (live-out [latex]-[/latex] def).

- Block 1 uses q, r, v before defining them [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] in(1) = {q, r, v}
- in(4) = {v, r} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(1) [latex]-[/latex] {q}) = {r, v}
- in(2) = {r, u} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(4) [latex]-[/latex] {v}) = {r, u}
- in(3) = {s, u} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(4) [latex]-[/latex] {q}) = {r, s, u, v}

Common: r, u

Answer: r, u

questions.text: The least number of temporary variables required to create a three-address code in static single assignment form for the expression q + r / 3 + s - t * 5 + u * v /w is _______________.
questions.solution:
In SSA every result gets a new variable. Count the operations:

t1 = r / 3, t2 = q + t1, t3 = t2 + s, t4 = t * 5, t5 = t3 [latex]-[/latex] t4, t6 = u * v, t7 = t6 / w, t8 = t5 + t7

8 operations [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 temporaries

Answer: 8

questions.text:
Consider an Entity-Relationship (ER) model in which entity sets E1 and E2 are connected by an m : n relationship R12. E1 and E3 are connected by a 1 : n (1 on the side of E1 and n on the side of E3) relationship R13.

E1 has two single-valued attributes a11 and a12 of which a11 is the key attribute. E2 has two single-valued attributes a21 and a22 of which a21 is the key attribute. E3 has two single-valued attributes a31 and a32 of which a31 is the key attribute. The relationships do not have any attributes.

If a relational model is derived from the above ER model, then the minimum number of relations that would be generated if all the relations are in 3NF is _______.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- E1(a11, a12), E2(a21, a22): one relation each
- R12 is m:n: needs its own relation (a11, a21)
- R13 is 1:n: add a11 as a foreign key in E3(a31, a32, a11), no separate table

Total = 4

Answer: 4

questions.text: Consider the DFAs M and N given above. The number of states in a minimal DFA that accepts the language L(M)[latex]\cap[/latex] L(N) is___________
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- M accepts strings ending with a.
- N accepts strings ending with b.

No string can end with both, so [latex]L(M)\cap L(N)=\emptyset[/latex]. The minimal DFA has a single non-accepting state.

Answer: 1

questions.text:
Consider the NPDA [latex]\langle Q=\{q_{0},q_{1},q_{2}\},[/latex] [latex]\Sigma =\{0,1\},[/latex] [latex]\Gamma =\{0,1,\perp \},\delta ,q_{0},\perp ,[/latex] [latex]F=\{q_{2}\} \rangle[/latex], where (as per usual convention) Q is the set of states, [latex]\Sigma[/latex] is the input alphabet, [latex]\Gamma[/latex] is the stack alphabet, [latex]\delta[/latex] is the state transition function, [latex]q_{0}[/latex] is the initial state, [latex]\perp[/latex] is the initial stack symbol, and [latex]F[/latex] is the set of accepting states. The state transition is as follows:

Which one of the following sequences must follow the string 101100 so that the overall string is accepted by the automaton?
questions.solution:
q0 pushes the input. It moves to q1 on one symbol or [latex]\epsilon[/latex] (an optional middle symbol). In q1, a 0 pops a 1 and a 1 pops a 0, so the second half must be the complement of the first half reversed.

Total length 6 + 5 = 11, so w = 10110 and the middle symbol is 0.
Reverse of w = 01101, complement = 10010.

Answer: 10010
